blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (Charge call to the payment provider has no timeout) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Charge is retried forever, without backoff, on a non-idempotent POST) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Pass an explicit `timeout=` (connect and read) to `requests.post`, so a provider that accepts the connection and never answers fails the call instead of holding the checkout worker forever; the timeout must then be handled by the bounded retry of R-ops-2.
findings.title: Charge call to the payment provider has no timeout

findings.recommendation: Bound the retries (a few attempts) with exponential backoff and jitter, retry only errors that are safe to retry (connection errors, 5xx/429 — not 4xx such as a declined card or a bad request, which `raise_for_status` also turns into a `RequestException`), and send an idempotency key derived from `order_id` so a retried POST cannot charge the order twice; after the last attempt, raise an error naming the order and the provider's status.
findings.title: Charge is retried forever, without backoff, on a non-idempotent POST

findings.recommendation: Log each failed attempt as a structured event — fields such as `order_id`, attempt number, HTTP status and exception class, without the request body or any credential — and log or raise the final failure, so an operator can see which orders fail and why.
findings.title: Provider errors are swallowed without a log

findings.recommendation: Read the provider URL from the environment or configuration (for example `PAYMENT_URL = os.environ["PAYMENT_URL"]`), so the sandbox the task verifies against and production use the same code.
findings.title: Payment provider URL is hard-coded
